text.text_excerpt: This place is a GEM for those who'd rather listen to good music than have frat boys puke on your shoes a few blocks over on Bourbon Street. I had a local friend show me around while visiting. Amazing. This place is the real deal. All the area musician's trickle in after their paid gigs have wrapped. The end of the night impromptu jam sessions are 'da best. It's a total dive in a neighborhood a little more gritty than most tourists would be comfortable in, but if you have your wits about you all should be fine. I think they even have a rice and beans special once a week. I missed it but heard it's down home and super yum.

This place is a little quirky but I liked it overall, mainly because it's a rare club in New Orleans where you can hear some serious straight ahead jazz and people actually listen to the music for the most part instead of yammering. I went on a Friday night to see Jesse McBride, so I'm not sure if it would be the same on other nights. The website says the music starts at 9, which in New Orleans generally means the music really starts at 10, 10:30 or 11. So we killed some time walking around the Quarter and entered at 9:30, only to find they were already on their third song. That was a surprise, but now we know. A bottle of Abita costs $5. One of my favorite live music venues anywhere. Really top-notch jazz where some of the best players in the world just drop in on Monday night after dinner. Tasty burgers too.
